name: 51. Raw Anthropic thinking rewrite must skip the latest assistant message (PR #6110)
description:
Bifrost's encrypted-reasoning fail-soft (core/encryptedreasoning.go) answers an upstream refusal of a replayed
reasoning payload by stripping the unverifiable parts and retrying once. On the raw Anthropic passthrough route
(/anthropic/v1/messages) that strip is stripRawAnthropicChatThinking, which edits the client's own bytes: it blanks
"signature" on thinking blocks and DROPS redacted_thinking blocks outright.

Anthropic forbids exactly that on one message. Per the Preserving thinking blocks rules
(https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#preserving-thinking-blocks): "Within the latest
assistant message, the sequence of consecutive thinking blocks must match what the model generated in the original
request: you can't rearrange, edit, or partially drop them. This includes redacted_thinking blocks." Violating it
returns a second 400 -- "`thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be
modified" -- so the client got a different, more confusing error than the one the retry was meant to heal, after a
wasted upstream call. Earlier turns carry no such rule ("Allowed: outside tool use, omit prior turns' thinking"),
so they are still rewritten.

Cases A and B pin that no request on this route ever earns the "cannot be modified" refusal, on the tool-result
round trip (the shape the Anthropic troubleshooting page names) and on a plain multi-turn replay. Case C is the
anti-over-skip guard: the unverifiable payload sits on an EARLIER assistant turn, so the fail-soft must still fire
and the request must succeed.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT -- do not "tidy" these bodies:
 - The protected turn must be the last message with role "assistant", which in case A is index 1, NOT the last
   array element. A fix that skips messages[len-1] instead of the last assistant message passes case B and still
   fails case A.
 - Case C needs a trailing assistant turn that carries NO thinking block, otherwise the payload under test would
   sit on the protected turn and the case would stop testing the earlier-turn path.
 - A 400 is NOT guarded away in the test scripts. After the fix, cases A and B are expected to return Anthropic's
   original "Invalid `data` in `redacted_thinking` block" refusal unretried; only the "cannot be modified"
   wording is a regression.

item.name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 /anthropic/v1/messages earlier-turn unverifiable redacted_thinking still degrades instead of 400 - PR #6110

exec: pm.test('an earlier assistant turn is still stripped so the fail-soft heals', function () {
pm.expect(body.toLowerCase(), 'the skip was applied too broadly and the retry edited the protected turn: ' + body).to.not.include('cannot be modified');

// Scoped to the error object rather than the raw body. This row enables thinking, and a SUCCESSFUL response may legitimately carry a redacted_thinking block in content: 'the API may return redacted_thinking blocks when portions of Claude's reasoning are safety-redacted' (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#redacted-thinking-blocks). A raw-text match reads that block as the rejection it is hunting for and fails the row at the exact moment the fail-soft worked. The rejection this looks for arrives as a 4xx error, which is where it is now read from - and the status assertion above already catches that case on its own, so this is the diagnostic, not the only guard.
pm.expect(err, 'Anthropic rejection reached the client; the encrypted-reasoning fail-soft did not fire on the earlier turn').to.not.include('redacted_thinking');
pm.expect(pm.response.json().content, 'no content returned after the stripped retry').to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty;
